rounds.text: The bear case centres on significant financial leverage and declining insider alignment, evidenced by a debt-to-equity ratio of 1.01x where borrowings exceed net worth [E32]. This structural risk is compounded by a persistent multi-year decline in promoter holding, which dropped from 74.41% in September 2023 to 64.91% by June 2026 [E35]. Furthermore, historical performance reveals a low median return on equity of 8% over ten years [E20], alongside an unsupportive 0.00% dividend yield despite reported profits [E4, E57]. Technical indicators also flash caution, highlighted by high annualised volatility of 53.7% [E48] and a severe historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -86.2% [E47], while screens flag that recent price growth is running far ahead of fundamental delivery [E51]. Conceded: the company demonstrates strong recent sales and profit momentum, including a trailing twelve-month profit growth of 216% and positive institutional money flow [E15, E38].

Conceded: debt-to-equity is 1.01x [E32], and promoter holding decreased by 9.50 percentage points to 64.91% [E35]. However, leverage risk is mitigated because borrowings actually decreased to Rs 259 Cr from Rs 275 Cr [E33], and profits are fully backed by cash with an operating cash flow of Rs 59 Cr and a cash conversion ratio of 1.18x [E28, E29]. While the 10-year median ROE was low at 8% [E20], returns have surged dramatically to a 21.6% ROE and 20.7% ROCE, with the last year's median ROE reaching 22% [E6, E7, E23]. Conceded: the dividend yield is 0.00% [E4], but retained earnings drove the total equity increase without any dilution [E86], funding strong operational growth. The bear's concern over high volatility and historical drawdown [E47, E48] ignores the company's exceptional 325.4% twelve-month return and a perfect relative-strength rating of 100 [E45, E46]. Finally, the claim that price growth outpaces fundamentals [E51] is contradicted by multi-year compounding where 5-year profit growth of 71% significantly outpaces a 52% share price growth [E13, E17, E50].

Conceded: borrowings decreased to Rs 259 Cr [E33] and operating cash flow reached Rs 59 Cr with a 1.18x conversion [E28, E29]. However, the bull's dismissal of the company's leverage ignores the reality that a debt-to-equity ratio of 1.01x still means total debt exceeds net worth, carrying genuine balance-sheet risk [E32]. Conceded: recent ROE and ROCE have surged to 21.6% and 20.7% respectively [E6, E7], but this must be weighed against a pedestrian 10-year median ROE of 8% [E20] and a low 3-year median ROE of 12% [E22, E58], demonstrating long-term historical mediocrity. Conceded: retained earnings have driven total equity without dilution [E86], yet the complete absence of a payout leaves investors with a 0.00% dividend yield [E4, E57]. The bull points to a 100 relative-strength rating and massive 12-month returns [E45, E46], but ignores the severe warning from the insider-bias checklist that the stock is extended at 89% of its 52-year range and that momentum is not an edge by itself [E42, E66]. Finally, while multi-year profit growth outpaced past price gains [E13, E17, E50], the screen explicitly warns that earnings growth is currently decelerating [E65] and that recent price growth has outpaced profit growth by 124%, leaving expectations running far ahead of delivery [E51].
